primary_diagnosis_treated: Sub‑optimal control of type 2 diabetes mellitus with intermittent ketosis

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after any change in renal function
medications.purpose: Control of essential hypertension and renal protection in diabetic nephropathy
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with albuminuria or hypertension (first‑line)

medications.dose: Individualised basal and prandial doses as per current regimen
medications.duration: Lifelong — dose adjusted based on glucose monitoring
medications.purpose: Glycaemic control in insulin‑treated type 2 diabetes
medications.nice_justification: NG28 recommends insulin when oral agents insufficient

medications.dose: Start 500 mg once daily with evening meal; increase to 500 mg twice daily after 1‑2 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually; dose may be increased to max 2000 mg/day
medications.purpose: First‑line oral glucose‑lowering therapy; improves insulin sensitivity
medications.nice_justification: NG28: Metformin MR is first‑line for all type 2 diabetes (eGFR >45 mL/min/1.73 m²) (first_line)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review renal function and ketone status every 6 months
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control, reduce albuminuria progression and cardiovascular risk in CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG28 & NG203: SGLT2i recommended alongside metformin for CKD with eGFR >45 (first_line)

medications.dose: Start 0.25 mg weekly; increase to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks, then to 1 mg after another 4‑6 weeks if tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review weight, HbA1c and gastrointestinal tolerance every 6 months
medications.purpose: Additional glucose lowering, weight loss and cardiovascular risk reduction in obese patient with CVD risk
medications.nice_justification: NG28: GLP‑1 RA preferred when CVD/obesity present (second_line)

medications.dose: 20 mg once daily in the evening
medications.duration: Lifelong — lipid panel at 4 weeks then annually
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (all CKD patients should receive a statin)
medications.nice_justification: NG203: Statin indicated for all CKD patients (first_line)

medications.duration: If QRISK ≥10 %: 12 months then reassess; otherwise not prescribed
medications.purpose: Primary prevention of cardiovascular events (pending QRISK assessment)
medications.nice_justification: NG28: Low‑dose aspirin considered for primary prevention after QRISK calculation

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive glucose‑lowering effect increases risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Reduce total insulin dose by 10‑20% on initiation of metformin and monitor fasting glucose closely

interactions_checked.interaction: Combined effect may precipitate euglycaemic diabetic ketoacidosis, especially during illness or reduced carbohydrate intake
interactions_checked.action: Educate patient on sick‑day rules, advise temporary insulin dose increase or drug hold if acutely unwell, monitor urine/serum ketones

interactions_checked.interaction: Both lower glucose; risk of hypoglycaemia
interactions_checked.action: Reduce basal insulin dose by ~30% when starting semaglutide; titrate based on glucose logs

interactions_checked.interaction: Slightly increased risk of gastrointestinal bleeding
interactions_checked.action: Consider gastro‑protection (e.g., PPI) if aspirin is started

assumptions_warnings: QRISK score not available – aspirin decision pending QRISK assessment.
Baseline lipid profile not provided – atorvastatin started assuming LDL‑C above target.
Allergy status not documented – assumed no hypersensitivity to proposed agents.
Intermittent ketosis noted; SGLT2i carries DKA risk – patient education and ketone monitoring required.
Liver function tests not supplied – assumed normal before initiating metformin, statin, and GLP‑1 RA.
treatment_summary: Add metformin MR and empagliflozin as first‑line oral agents for glycaemic control and renal protection, introduce semaglutide for additional glucose lowering, weight loss and CV risk reduction, start atorvastatin for CKD‑related cardiovascular risk, and consider low‑dose aspirin after QRISK assessment. Continue lisinopril and insulin with dose adjustments to mitigate hypoglycaemia. Monitor HbA1c, eGFR, ACR, potassium, lipids, weight, blood pressure and ketones per NICE NG28/NG203. Provide lifestyle advice (diet, exercise, smoking cessation, structured diabetes education).
